content:
Apple has shared more details about the AI labeling requirements it announced for Apple Music back in March. Here are the details.

AI-generated content will be clearly labeled on Apple Music

Apple announced earlier this year that Apple Music will require AI transparency disclosures for new artwork, songs, compositions, and music videos uploaded to the platform.

Now, the company has further explained how this measure will work.

In an email sent to creators today, Apple stated: "Later this year, we will also make these markers visible to Apple Music users in the form of a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple has also clarified the circumstances under which disclosures are required. The email reads as follows:

Apple Music added that the goal of this measure is "to provide maximum transparency to listeners," and asked creators to refer to their Music Style Guide for more information.

Apple Music's approach is only the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the surge of AI-generated music—an increasing number of artists are incorporating generative AI into their production processes.

Spotify previously stated that it would, by default, exclude music from AI Personas from its editorial and algorithmic recommendations; Deezer announced last year that songs entirely generated by AI will not be included in recommendations or editorial playlists. Deezer also revealed last month that music entirely generated by AI accounted for over half of newly uploaded music per day for the first time.

Taking Apple Music as an example, platform head Oliver Schusser mentioned earlier when appearing on Billboard's 'On the Record' podcast that, although over a third of the music uploaded to Apple Music each month is entirely AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of plays on the platform.
